newsitem.title: USA: BioSafe landfill permit in Mass. upheld.
newsitem.headline: BioSafe landfill permit in Mass. upheld.

text.p: BioSafe International Inc said on Wednesday that a Massachusetts judge upheld the Department of Environmental Protection's move to grant Fairhaven, Mass., a permit for BioSafe to remodel the town's landfill.
A group of 16 Fairhaven residents challenged the state agency's decision to issue the permit in 1995, BioSafe said.

Biosafe, however, said the delays and uncertainty associated with the project prevented the company from making additional capital investments and the company has been operating the landfill at a reduced capacity.

This landfill remodeling project has the potential to create 1.5 million cubic yards of new capacity for future disposal and to generate more than $50 million in revenues for BioSafe, the company said.
Pending a possible appeal and other litigation, BioSafe said it will continue to reassess various alternative for the Fairhaven landfill remodeling project.
Judge Phillip Rivard-Rapoza found that the permit sufficiently addressed the potential odor and dust conditions and did not violate any setback requirements for the landfill.
